newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends higher, new crop outpaces old crop.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends higher, new crop outpaces old crop.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed higher, with new crop particularly strong amid some talk of a possible switch into acreage in Canada from canola to spring wheat, floor sources said.
They also noted commodity fund long liquidation amid bearish technicals helped to limit gains in old crop July.

Strong wheat prices in the U.S. following freeze damage to crops in Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas, was seen possibly prompting a switch in Canadian planting plans from canola to spring wheat. "If U.S. wheat prices remain strong we may see increased wheat acres (in Canada) this year," one dealer said.
Old-crop July ended $1.50 higher at $421.40 while new-crop November finished up $7.20 at $374.20. July flaxseed ended up $3.50 at $346.50 on commercial buying.

Western barley closed higher, boosted by stronger CBOT grains, although a pick up in producer selling helped to limit gains. July finished up $1.50 at $140.50. Wheat was also firm with July up $2.60 at $169.60.
Feed peas and oats remained tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas, oats)
